property_summary: For every input where the callee reverts when asked to transfer the smaller (unmultiplied) amount but succeeds when asked the larger 1e18-scaled amount, the reference contract always returns true (call succeeds) while the mutant can return false (call fails); the test fuzzes amounts and recipient and uses a helper callee that conditionally reverts for smaller amounts so the mutant is distinguishable.

For any recipient list and amounts, the reference C always successfully completes transfer (returns true / does not revert) when its callee accepts calls for amounts equal to v * 1e18, while the mutant that sends v instead of v * 1e18 can fail (revert) for some fuzzed v when the callee requires the larger scaled amount — we assert that calling transfer does not revert on the reference for all admissible inputs routed through a helper that enforces a minimum required amount, and the mutant will revert for some inputs.

For any caller and arrays, C.transfer never reverts (returns true) when the callee accepts calls that require amounts >= v*1e18; the mutant that sends v instead of v*1e18 can cause the external call to revert for some fuzzed v and recipient, breaking the universal non-revert property.

For every fuzzed recipient array length (>=1) and per-recipient uint amount v_i, C.transfer never reverts (always returns true) when interacting with a callee that accepts calls only if the forwarded amount equals v * 1e18; the mutant that forwards v (without 1e18 scaling) will revert for some fuzzed v/recipient causing the universal non-revert property to fail.

For any caller and non-empty arrays, the reference C.forwarding behavior always returns true (does not revert) when the callee accepts calls that require the forwarded amount to be v * 1e18; the mutant that forwards v (without multiplying by 1e18) can cause the external call to revert for some fuzzed v/recipient, breaking the universal non-revert property.

For every input where the external callee call returns success, the reference contract's transfer returns true (call completes successfully and the test observes success), whereas the mutant inverts the check and will revert when the callee returns success; thus the reference always reports success for successful callee responses but the mutant fails for some inputs where the callee succeeds.
